This allows treating them as equivalent without loss of generality. The identification process simplifies notation and proof structures, especially when dealing with higher-order products. In GSI, this translates to treating different representations of joint probability distributions as equivalent under isomorphism, enabling modular Bayesian updating. For GSE, it supports seamless transitions between state-space decompositions, where each decomposition corresponds to a valid grouping of variables. The failure mode arises when such isomorphisms do not preserve relevant topological or measure-theoretic properties, leading to incorrect conclusions in probabilistic or dynamical systems modeling.
